title: Freelance parents can now pause national pension premiums without losing pension credit
summary: Japan started a new childcare exemption on October 1 for eligible National Pension Category 1 parents raising a child under age one. Walang income test, and covered months still count as paid months toward the basic old-age pension.
why_it_matters: For self-employed, freelance and other Category 1 parents, this is direct household cash-flow relief without reducing future basic pension credit for the covered months.

claims.text: From October 1, 2026, eligible National Pension Category 1 parents raising a child under age one can receive a childcare-period premium exemption with no income requirement.
Covered months are treated as premium-paid months for old-age basic pension calculation, and both parents can qualify if each is Category 1 and meets the rules.
The FY2026 standard National Pension premium is ¥17,920 per month.
At the FY2026 rate, 12 exempt months correspond to ¥215,040 of gross premium relief in a full-12-month case; actual relief depends on eligible months and annual premium rates.
The scheme narrows a parental-support gap for people outside employee pension coverage by pairing current premium relief with preserved basic pension accrual.

content.key_message: Kung Category 1 National Pension payer ka at may anak na wala pang isang taon, check this now: eligible months can be exempt without sacrificing basic pension credit.
content.whats_new: The childcare-period exemption is now live. Eligible Category 1 parents can receive relief from October 2026 onward, including remaining eligible months for some children born before launch who are still under one.
content.skeptical_view: Hindi ito blanket free pension for parents. It is limited to Category 1 insured parents who meet the parent-child and same-address rules, and the eligible period differs by case.
what_next: Check whether your case requires filing instead of assuming the exemption is automatic.
If premiums were already paid for covered months, confirm the official credit/refund treatment.
content.recommendation: Eligible Category 1 parents should verify their status and file promptly through an official Japan Pension Service channel when filing is required.
content.what_would_change_mind: A material eligibility or implementation revision by MHLW or Japan Pension Service.

30 sec: A new National Pension childcare exemption started October 1.
Eligible Category 1 parents can stop paying for covered months while those months still count as paid for basic pension.
Check whether filing is required in your case.
reading_levels.2_min: The new exemption targets National Pension Category 1 insured people such as many self-employed and freelance workers. Eligible parents raising a child under one can have covered premiums waived regardless of income, while those months remain credited for old-age basic pension calculation. The maximum period can reach 12 months in specified cases; birth mothers with maternity exemption generally transition into nine months of childcare exemption.

outcomes: Identify whether the exemption is relevant to your pension category.
Explain why this differs from simply not paying a pension premium.
learning.background: National Pension Category 1 generally covers people such as self-employed workers, farmers, students and unemployed people outside employee pension coverage. The new rule adds a childcare-period exemption through the child's first year while preserving pension credit for covered months.

terms.meaning: A National Pension member generally outside employee pension coverage.
terms.why_it_matters: This exemption is specifically for Category 1.

how_it_works.title: Eligibility
how_it_works.explanation: The parent must be Category 1 insured, have a qualifying parent-child relationship, and share the child's registered address. There is no income test.

how_it_works.title: Premium relief
how_it_works.explanation: Eligible premiums are waived for the covered childcare period.

how_it_works.title: Pension credit
how_it_works.explanation: Covered months still count as premium-paid months for old-age basic pension calculation.

learning.example: ESTIMATE: at ¥17,920 per month, a full 12-month case corresponds to ¥215,040 in gross premiums. Actual relief can differ.
takeaways: Both parents can qualify if each meets the rules.
Covered months still count as paid for basic pension.
Do not assume filing is automatic.

action_plan.goal: Secure the exemption for eligible months.
action_plan.who_should_act: Category 1 National Pension insured parents with a child under one who meet the official eligibility rules.
action_plan.deadline: File promptly after meeting the eligibility conditions when filing is required.
prepare: Check your pension category and the official eligibility page.

steps.action: Confirm Category 1 status, qualifying parent-child relationship, and same registered address.
steps.how: Use the Japan Pension Service childcare-exemption guidance.
steps.done_when: The official conditions match your case.

steps.action: Confirm whether your case needs a notification.
steps.how: Use Japan Pension Service guidance; some birth mothers can be processed without a new filing, while other cases require filing.
steps.done_when: You know whether your case is automatic or requires filing.

steps.how: Japan Pension Service allows electronic filing through MyNaPortal or paper filing through the National Pension desk of the registered municipality; postal filing is also available.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming every parent qualifies regardless of pension category.
Treating the exemption as a pension-credit gap.

decision_rules.then: Use the pension/support rules that apply to your category instead of this scheme.

action_plan.follow_up: Confirm the exemption outcome and any treatment of premiums already paid for approved months.
